qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High customer switching costs in Wealth Management ($9.3T client assets across Wealth and Investment Management, >95% annual client retention). Ad-valorem fee model provides structural pricing power scaling with asset inflation, though institutional trading and underwriting remain competitive and cyclical.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Fortress Balance Sheet & Cash Conversion, REJECT). Morgan Stanley has successfully transformed into a wealth management powerhouse (~54% of revenue from Wealth and Investment Management), but remains a Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB) with >$1.3T in assets, substantial institutional securities operations, and massive financial leverage (long-term debt >$250B vs net income of $13B-$17B). The capital structure is inherently dependent on wholesale funding, repo markets, and regulatory support, failing the Munger peace-of-mind fortress balance sheet standard.
qualitative.evidence: FY 2025 net revenue reached $70.65B (Institutional Securities $33.08B / 46.8%, Wealth Management $31.75B / 44.9%, Investment Management $6.53B / 9.2%). Net income was $16.86B ($13.39B in FY 2024), ROTCE was 21.6% (18.8% in FY 2024), and ROE was ~15.6%. Total assets scale past $1.3T, funded by over $250B in long-term debt and hundreds of billions in repo liabilities and deposits. Free cash flow conversion is structurally volatile/unsuited for dealer banks. Fails Gate 6 on systemic financial leverage and debt/net income > 4.0x.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
